title: Kayla Hamilton Act

claims.claim: The Kayla Hamilton Act tightens the placement process for unaccompanied migrant children in federal custody
claims.sourceSpan: may not make a placement determination
claims.note: "migrant" is a neutral gloss for the source term "unaccompanied alien child"; federal custody + placement-process rewrite is sourced.

claims.claim: requires HHS to place children 12 and older in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings
claims.sourceSpan: the unaccompanied alien child shall be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings
claims.note: Mandatory ("shall be placed"), age-scoped to 12 or older ("12 years of age or older").

claims.claim: if they are a flight risk or a danger
claims.sourceSpan: is a flight risk; or

claims.claim: including if they have gang-related tattoos or markings
claims.sourceSpan: has a gang-related tattoo or any other gang-related marking

claims.claim: a conviction for a serious criminal offense or aggravated felony
claims.sourceSpan: has been convicted of a serious criminal offense

claims.claim: or a gang-related arrest, charge, or conviction
claims.sourceSpan: for conduct in connection with gang affiliation or gang activity
claims.note: Gang modifier correctly attached only to the arrest/charge/conviction category, not to the serious-offense/agg-felony convictions.

claims.claim: prohibits placing any child with an individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who is not a United States citizen or a lawful permanent resident of the United States

claims.claim: or who — or an adult in whose household — has been convicted of certain sex, trafficking, domestic-violence, child-abuse, murder, or felony offenses
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who has been convicted of, or who resides in a household with an individual who has been convicted of
claims.note: Hedged with "certain"; list matches enumerated (I)-(XI).

claims.claim: requires HHS to give DHS detailed background information on all adult household members at any placement home
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide to the Secretary of Homeland Security, with regard to the individual with whom the child will be placed and each adult resident of the individual's household

claims.claim: Requires secure-facility placement for unaccompanied migrant children 12 and older who are a flight risk or danger
claims.sourceSpan: the unaccompanied alien child shall be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings

claims.claim: including those with gang-related indicators or serious criminal convictions
claims.sourceSpan: has a gang-related tattoo or any other gang-related marking

claims.claim: bars placement with any individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident or who has certain criminal convictions
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who is not a United States citizen or a lawful permanent resident of the United States

claims.claim: mandates sharing of household adult background information with DHS
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide to the Secretary of Homeland Security

claims.claim: Secure Facility for Gang-Affiliated Minors
claims.sourceSpan: the unaccompanied alien child shall be placed in a secure facility
claims.note: Headline narrows to "gang-affiliated"; the secure-facility trigger is actually flight-risk OR danger for any child 12+, with gang affiliation only one example of danger. Subs clarify. Topical label, not material.

claims.claim: Before placing an unaccompanied child 12 or older, HHS must contact the child's home country consulate or embassy to request any relevant arrest records, pending charges, or conviction documents
claims.sourceSpan: contact the consulate or embassy of the country of citizenship, nationality, or last habitual residence for the unaccompanied alien child to obtain any relevant arrest records, pending criminal charges, or conviction documents

claims.claim: HHS must also examine the child for gang-related tattoos and markings
claims.sourceSpan: conduct an examination of the unaccompanied alien child

claims.claim: If the child is a flight risk or a danger — including having a gang-related tattoo or marking, a conviction for a serious criminal offense or aggravated felony, or a gang-related arrest, pending charge, or conviction — HHS must place them in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings
claims.sourceSpan: shall be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings

claims.claim: Sponsor Vetting Requirements
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall not place an unaccompanied alien child in the custody of any individual

claims.claim: No child may be placed with any individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, or who — or an adult resident of whose household — has been convicted of certain sex, trafficking, domestic-violence, child-abuse, murder, or felony offenses
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who is not a United States citizen or a lawful permanent resident of the United States

claims.claim: Before placement, HHS must share with DHS: names, Social Security or individual taxpayer identification numbers, dates of birth, addresses, immigration status, contact information, and background-check results for all adult residents of the placement household
claims.sourceSpan: the social security number or individual taxpayer identification number of the individual and each adult resident of the individual's household

claims.claim: Required background checks include, at a minimum, an investigation of the Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Website, a public records background check, and a national criminal history background check based on fingerprints for every adult in the household
claims.sourceSpan: which shall include at a minimum an investigation of the Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Website, a public records background check, and a national criminal history background check based on fingerprints

claims.claim: Names the Act the "Kayla Hamilton Act"
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the ``Kayla Hamilton Act''.

claims.claim: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect
claims.sourceSpan: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

claims.claim: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 279(b)(2))
claims.sourceSpan: Section 462(b)(2) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 279(b)(2)) is amended

claims.claim: so the Office of Refugee Resettlement Director makes unaccompanied-child placement determinations
claims.sourceSpan: The Director of the Office of Refugee Resettlement shall make determinations under paragraph (1)(C)

claims.claim: in accordance with 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(2)
claims.sourceSpan: in accordance with section 235(c)(2) of the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 (8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(2))

claims.claim: Conforming amendment tying ORR's placement authority to the safe-and-secure-placement standard rewritten by Section 3
claims.sourceSpan: Safe and secure placements
claims.note: Sec. 2 points to 235(c)(2), which Sec. 3 rewrites as "Safe and secure placements."

claims.claim: Before any placement, HHS must consult with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall consult with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General

claims.claim: to help ensure the child appears at immigration hearings
claims.sourceSpan: to ensure that the unaccompanied alien child will appear for all immigration, administrative, and judicial hearings or proceedings

claims.claim: is protected from smugglers, traffickers, and gangs
claims.sourceSpan: will be protected from smugglers, traffickers, gangs, and others

claims.claim: and to determine flight risk, danger, and criminal history
claims.sourceSpan: is a danger to self, another individual, or the community

claims.claim: children in HHS custody are otherwise to be placed in the least restrictive setting in their best interest
claims.sourceSpan: shall be promptly placed in the least restrictive setting that is in the best interest of the child

claims.claim: and may not be released on their own recognizance
claims.sourceSpan: An unaccompanied alien child may not be released on his or her own recognizance

claims.claim: The consultation and least-restrictive-setting rules apply to all unaccompanied children
claims.sourceSpan: may not make a placement determination under this paragraph for an unaccompanied alien child
claims.note: Consultation (A)(i) and least-restrictive (B)(i) carry no age limit.

claims.claim: the consulate-records request, gang examination, and secure-facility placement apply only to children 12 or older
claims.sourceSpan: In the case of an unaccompanied alien child 12 years of age or older

claims.claim: For unaccompanied migrant children aged 12 and older, requires HHS to request arrest records, pending charges, and conviction documents from the child's home country consulate or embassy
claims.sourceSpan: contact the consulate or embassy of the country of citizenship, nationality, or last habitual residence for the unaccompanied alien child to obtain any relevant arrest records, pending criminal charges, or conviction documents

claims.claim: and conduct an examination for gang-related tattoos and markings before making any placement
claims.sourceSpan: conduct an examination of the unaccompanied alien child

claims.claim: A child 12 or older must be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings (and, if ordered removed, until removal) if the child is a flight risk or a danger to self, others, or the community
claims.sourceSpan: shall be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings (and, if ordered removed, until such unaccompanied alien child is removed)

claims.claim: including having a gang-related tattoo or marking, a conviction for a serious criminal offense or aggravated felony, or, for gang-related conduct, an arrest record, pending charge, other pending proceeding, or conviction
claims.sourceSpan: any arrest record; ``(bb) any pending criminal charge; ``(cc) any other pending proceeding; or ``(dd) any conviction

claims.claim: Children younger than 12 are exempt from the gang-screening and consulate-records requirements
claims.sourceSpan: In the case of an unaccompanied alien child 12 years of age or older
claims.note: Contrapositive of the 12-or-older scope; screening obligations attach only to 12+.

claims.claim: Prohibits placement of any unaccompanied child with an individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident
claims.sourceSpan: shall not place an unaccompanied alien child in the custody of any individual who is one or more of the following

claims.claim: or who — or an adult resident of whose household — has been convicted of an enumerated offense
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who has been convicted of, or who resides in a household with an individual who has been convicted of

claims.claim: and requires HHS to transmit detailed household information to DHS before completing any placement
claims.sourceSpan: Before placing a child with any individual, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide to the Secretary of Homeland Security

claims.claim: Required information includes names, Social Security or individual taxpayer identification numbers, dates of birth, addresses, immigration status, contact information, and background-check results for all adult residents of the proposed placement household
claims.sourceSpan: the name of the individual and each adult resident of the individual's household

claims.claim: Background checks must include, at a minimum, an investigation of the Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Website, a public records background check, and a national criminal history background check based on fingerprints
claims.sourceSpan: which shall include at a minimum an investigation of the Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Website, a public records background check, and a national criminal history background check based on fingerprints

claims.claim: The enumerated categories of prohibited individuals include those convicted of a sex offense, severe trafficking, domestic violence, child abuse, murder or manslaughter, an aggravated felony, any felony, or any crime punishable by more than 1 year
claims.sourceSpan: a sex offense (as defined in section 111(5) of the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act
claims.note: Non-exhaustive ("include"); also omits (VI) child-sexual-abuse-material and (VII) INA 236(c)(1) custody crimes, acceptable under "include."

claims.claim: plus any other offense the Attorney General designates in the Attorney General's sole and unreviewable discretion
claims.sourceSpan: any other criminal offense as designated by the Attorney General, in the Attorney General's sole and unreviewable discretion

claims.claim: Provides that nothing in the Act requires DHS, HHS, the State Department, or the Attorney General to comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act
claims.sourceSpan: to require the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Secretary of State, or the Attorney General to comply with the requirements of chapter 35 of title 44

claims.claim: or to conduct APA notice-and-comment rulemaking
claims.sourceSpan: to promulgate regulations under subchapter II of chapter 5 of title 5

claims.claim: if those officials determine compliance would impede immediate implementation
claims.sourceSpan: if such individuals determine that compliance would impede the immediate implementation of this Act

claims.claim: Lets the implementing agencies bypass Paperwork Reduction Act review (chapter 35 of title 44) and APA rulemaking (subchapter II of chapter 5 of title 5) at their own determination
claims.sourceSpan: the requirements of chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code (commonly referred to as the ``Paperwork Reduction Act'')

claims.claim: Takes effect on enactment
claims.sourceSpan: this Act and the amendments made by this shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: and applies to release and custody determinations that are pending or occur on or after enactment
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any release and custody determinations for an unaccompanied alien child (as defined in section 642(g)(2) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002), that are pending or occur on or after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: and to all release redeterminations
claims.sourceSpan: and all release redeterminations

claims.claim: Reaches unaccompanied-alien-child cases already in progress at enactment, not only new ones
claims.sourceSpan: that are pending or occur on or after the date of the enactment of this Act
claims.note: "already in progress" = "pending."

claims.claim: Section 5 — Paperwork Reduction Act / Administrative Procedure Act Exemption
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 5. EXEMPTION FROM PAPERWORK REDUCTION ACT AND THE ADMINISTRATIVE

claims.claim: Lets DHS, HHS, the State Department, and the Attorney General skip Paperwork Reduction Act review and Administrative Procedure Act notice-and-comment rulemaking whenever those officials themselves determine that compliance would impede immediate implementation of the Act
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Secretary of State, or the Attorney General to comply with the requirements of chapter 35 of title 44

claims.claim: this separate section removes the ordinary procedural checks on how the new placement rules are implemented, at the agencies' own discretion — a structural change absent from the short title and stated purpose
claims.sourceSpan: if such individuals determine that compliance would impede the immediate implementation
claims.note: Fair structural synthesis; the short title/purpose ("combat the trafficking of children") does not mention the PRA/APA carve-out.

claims.claim: The bill requires HHS to contact a child's home country consulate for a criminal record before placement, but does not establish a timeline for how long HHS may hold a child while awaiting a response, or what happens if the consulate does not respond
claims.sourceSpan: contact the consulate or embassy of the country of citizenship, nationality, or last habitual residence
claims.note: Premise sourced; absence of any response-timeline provision is accurate.

claims.claim: The bill bars placement with any individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident but does not address what happens to a child if no eligible placement is available, potentially requiring prolonged secure-facility detention
claims.sourceSpan: An individual who is not a United States citizen or a lawful permanent resident of the United States
claims.note: Premise sourced; no-eligible-placement contingency is genuinely absent from source.

claims.claim: Mandatory consulate/embassy arrest-record request for unaccompanied children aged 12 and older before placement
claims.sourceSpan: contact the consulate or embassy of the country of citizenship, nationality, or last habitual residence for the unaccompanied alien child to obtain any relevant arrest records

claims.claim: Mandatory gang tattoo and marking examination before placement for children aged 12 and older
claims.sourceSpan: conduct an examination of the unaccompanied alien child

claims.claim: Mandatory secure-facility placement for children aged 12 and older who are a flight risk or danger, including those with gang indicators or serious-offense/aggravated-felony convictions
claims.sourceSpan: the unaccompanied alien child shall be placed in a secure facility for the duration of any immigration proceedings

claims.claim: Prohibition on placement with any individual who is not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, or who (or a household member) has an enumerated criminal conviction
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall not place an unaccompanied alien child in the custody of any individual

claims.claim: Requirement to transmit household adult background check results to DHS before each placement
claims.sourceSpan: the results of all background and criminal records checks conducted on the individual and each adult resident of the individual's household

claims.claim: Mandatory pre-placement consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General to assess appearance at hearings, protection from traffickers and gangs, and flight risk, danger, and criminal history
claims.sourceSpan: shall consult with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General

claims.claim: Express prohibition on releasing an unaccompanied alien child on his or her own recognizance
claims.sourceSpan: An unaccompanied alien child may not be released on his or her own recognizance

claims.claim: Exemption letting DHS, HHS, State, and the Attorney General bypass the Paperwork Reduction Act and Administrative Procedure Act where compliance would impede immediate implementation
claims.sourceSpan: if such individuals determine that compliance would impede the immediate implementation of this Act

claims.claim: Applies to release and custody determinations pending or occurring on or after enactment, and to all release redeterminations
claims.sourceSpan: that are pending or occur on or after the date of the enactment of this Act, and all release redeterminations

claims.claim: 6 U.S.C. 279(b)(2): rewritten so ORR placement determinations for unaccompanied alien children are made in accordance with 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(2)
